title: When the Regiment Falls
premise: In 1911 on a humid colonial port, Lena Nystrom, daughter of a drowned pearl diver and indentured to the Meridian Trading Company, has learned that survival means invisibility. When an infant is abandoned at the company warehouse with a ledger page sewn into his swaddling — proof that Meridian has been falsifying deaths to claim divers' inheritance shares — Lena cannot unsee it. Smuggling the child and the page past three checkpoints to the colonial magistrate, she discovers the boy is her half-brother, the son her father never told her of, and that the company's clerk who left him is her father's old partner. At the third checkpoint, betrayed by the one ally she trusted, Lena must choose between reclaiming her own indenture and burning the evidence to save the boy; she chooses the boy, testifies at the cost of her freedom, and ends the novel years later, freed and rootless, teaching the boy to dive in waters she no longer belongs to but no longer fears.
about_author: Petra Okafor is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trading-company ledgers in Southeast Asian port archives. She writes historical fiction about the people those ledgers recorded only as numbers.

chapters.title: Salt in the Lungs
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Opens with her diving the shallows before her indenture shift, remembering her father's drowning. Establishes the port, the Meridian compound, and her philosophy of busy hands and a closed mouth. Emotional beat: grief worn as competence.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Name
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She is summoned by the head clerk, who mispronounces her father's name and deducts her mother's debt against her wages. Introduces the ledger room where she works and the arithmetic of inherited debt. Emotional beat: quiet fury converted into precision.

chapters.title: Left at the Door
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, night shift. A crying bundle appears at the warehouse door; a figure in the fog — the clerk Voss — says only 'forget the face' and vanishes. Inside the swaddling she finds a torn ledger page. Emotional beat: terror and a terrible recognition of choice.

chapters.title: What the Page Says
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. By lamplight she deciphers the page: diver deaths recorded as debts forgiven, shares quietly absorbed by Meridian. Her father's name appears twice. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering her grief was bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She maps the route to the magistrate: the harbor gate, the customs house, the company's own counting-room checkpoint. Introduces Sefa, a dockside cook who owes her father, as a potential ally. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into a plan.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Doesn't Cry
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Hiding the infant in the drying lofts, she notices his eyes — the same grey-green as her own, as her father's. Denial, then a search through her mother's old letters. Emotional beat: the possibility of family as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: Sefa's Debt
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Flashback to the night Lena's father died and what Voss ordered hushed. Sefa agrees to hide the boy for two days but warns her: Voss is not saving the child, he is saving himself. Emotional beat: loyalty shadowed by doubt.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A surprise audit of the ledger room; she palms a second page under the auditor's nose while the baby's blanket fibers cling to her sleeve. Nearly caught by the head clerk. Emotional beat: the thrill and cost of becoming someone who steals.

chapters.title: The Face She Must Forget
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He watches Lena from the counting room, knowing she has the page, gambling that his old promise to her father will hold. Reveals his history: the two men were partners before Meridian bought them both. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as caution.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Harbor Gate
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She passes the harbor gate with the page sewn into her diving belt, the boy drugged with poppy syrup in a fish crate Sefa arranged. A guard she grew up with waves her through — then asks one question too many. Emotional beat: relief that curdles.

chapters.title: The Head Clerk's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Head clerk Brandt's POV. He has found the missing page's twin in the company's duplicate books and begins closing the net, less from loyalty than from terror of his own signature on the falsified entries. Emotional beat: cowardice as an engine of cruelty.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The customs officer is a woman, Madame Reyes, who once dove for pearls herself. She recognizes the belt, recognizes the lie, and lets Lena pass with a whispered warning: someone has already described her to the magistrate's own clerks. Emotional beat: sisterhood across the colonial line.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Smoke
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Meridian's men come to the cookhouse; Sefa, to protect his own family, tells them about the fish crate. He keeps the boy hidden anyway, buying hours with his silence. Emotional beat: the unbearable mathematics of survival.

chapters.title: What Her Father Promised
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He intercepts Lena before the third checkpoint and tells her the truth: the boy is her father's son by a diver Voss loved; the page was meant to reach the magistrate years ago. He offers her escape passage instead of testimony. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as a burden handed off.

chapters.title: Rootless
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A night of decision in the drying lofts: take the passage and vanish, or walk into the counting room and burn the duplicate ledgers that would let Meridian survive her testimony. She remembers her father teaching her to hold her breath past fear. Emotional beat: the stillness before the dive.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Counting Room
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She walks into Meridian's own checkpoint carrying the boy openly, a diversion while Sefa's nephew sets the duplicate ledgers alight in the archive. Brandt seizes her; the fire alarms scatter the guards. Emotional beat: sacrifice staged as surrender.

chapters.title: The Burning Ledger
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. The counting room burns; Brandt chooses to save his own signature pages and thereby destroys the company's only defense. He flees the port. Emotional beat: a coward's victory that becomes the truth's.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Before the magistrate she testifies with the surviving page and Voss's corroboration; her indenture is voided, but she is bound to the port pending inquiry — free and unfree at once. The boy is placed in her care. Emotional beat: justice that arrives incomplete.

chapters.title: Shares and Shadows
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The inquiry drags; divers' families begin claiming their shares. Some thank her; others blame her for the fire that destroyed records that named their own debts. Emotional beat: belonging refused by every side.

chapters.title: Voss at the Gate
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He leaves on the morning boat, pausing at the harbor gate to leave her their father's old diving knife and a confession he cannot speak aloud. Lena watches from the lofts and does not go down. Emotional beat: forgiveness withheld, grief released.

chapters.title: The Long Breath
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Climax of the inner arc: called to name her price for silence about the magistrate's own clerks, she instead reads the surviving page aloud in the public square, giving the divers' families the whole truth at the cost of her protection. Emotional beat: choosing the community over safety, finally belonging to no one but herself and the boy.

chapters.title: Water She No Longer Fears
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, years later. On a different coast, she teaches the boy — her brother — to dive, holding him under just past fear, the way her father taught her. The ledger page is framed in a fisherman's chapel; her name is not on it, and she no longer needs it to be. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed from debt into gift.
